crime: Every evening until the light went, a girl sat by the courtyard fountain and sketched {WITCH_NAME}. Of all her sitters, she said, {WITCH_NAME} was the only one who never moved.
One day before supper, the girl closed her sketchbook and smiled. "I've drawn you enough. Tomorrow I'll draw someone else."

When {WITCH_NAME} was small, one ink blot on a school form had been enough. Her mother sat her on a station bench with her packed case and boarded the train alone, then stepped off just as the doors closed. "Next time I won't." From then on, {WITCH_NAME} sat still and never slipped up again.

Now she pushed the girl's face into the basin and laid her palm on the girl's back. Fixed by that hand, the girl stayed under the water until she drowned. Then {WITCH_NAME} sat the dead girl on the rim, bent her over the open sketchbook, lifted the girl's hand with the charcoal in it, and fixed her in place.

She came into the dining hall alone for supper, and afterward played pool in the recreation room among the others. From after supper until dusk, prisoners looking down from the upper railing saw the girl on the rim, bent over her book, as on every evening. At dusk, standing at the railing among them, {WITCH_NAME} released her from the Magic, and the girl tipped into the basin before their eyes.

In the trial court, the prisoners took it that the girl had fallen in at dusk while {WITCH_NAME} stood among them. But the prisoner who pulled her from the water had found her stiff and still bent in a sitting position, her hand raised and clutching the charcoal. Then they understood: the girl had been dead since before supper, held upright on the rim by {WITCH_NAME}'s hand.
fields.epitaph: She never once moved, and it never once kept anyone.
execution: An iron track rose, ending in a buffer stop. Between the rails, backed against the buffer, sat an iron station bench, and the witch was chained to it.
She sat perfectly still with her packed case on her knees.
An iron train rolled in along the track and did not stop. Its iron front pressed her and the bench into the buffer.
Then the train stood against the buffer, and she sat still between its iron front and the stop.

magic.name: Stay Put
magic.text: She can fix anyone or anything she touches in place against any force but her own.
